$comment: workhub-owned metadata about the plugins in marketplace.json: how much this vault needs each one, and the scope it is installed at. Claude Code does not read this file - the app's Plugins tab does, because the classification exists nowhere else in machine-readable form (docs/plugins.md states it in prose). `tier` is decided by what breaks without the plugin: `required` = an app feature or an agent launch stops working - only workhub, whose skills the app names in its own launch prompts and whose harness hooks are the sole readers of the .claude/project-context.json the app writes; `recommended` = nothing breaks but the harness is noticeably worse; `optional` = a matter of taste or tech stack. `scope` is where the plugin is meant to be installed, not what it depends on: `user` is the default because a plugin is switched on per machine and works from any directory, and a hook that needs a vault or a project config gates itself on that file existing rather than on being installed narrowly. `project` is left for what would be actively wrong outside one repository. Deliberately carries no version/description/author: plugin.json is the single source for those (T-0221). Every plugin in marketplace.json must appear here exactly once, and vice versa; src/lib/plugin-catalog.test.ts fails CI when the two drift.

plugins.name: workhub
plugins.summary: Task board, vault knowledge base, schedule/mindmap editing, long-term memory, the app's release procedure, and the harness hooks that carry the app's registered projects and their rules into a session. Meaningless outside a vault, and gated on one.

plugins.name: engineering
plugins.summary: Development workflow: role-based sub-agents, the commit/PR/ADR/TDD skills, serena/context7 MCP launchers. How a team commits and branches is a team's own call, so this is a recommendation - nothing in the app stops working without it.

plugins.name: claude-tooling
plugins.summary: Extending Claude Code itself. Its SessionStart notice reports outdated plugins across every marketplace - the Plugins tab now answers the same question for this one.

plugins.name: authoring
plugins.summary: Writing text deliverables and handing them over: README, CLAUDE.md, release notes, work logs, posting to Slack.

plugins.name: visuals
plugins.summary: Visual deliverables as self-contained HTML, and the PDF handed over: fixed 16:9 slide decks rendered in the session, and publication-quality PDF export for decks and documents alike.

plugins.name: agent-ops
plugins.summary: Running agents in a terminal multiplexer (herdr/zellij) and the setup behind it.

plugins.name: zenn
plugins.summary: Zenn tech-blog writing: house style and Zenn-flavoured markdown.

plugins.name: strategy
plugins.summary: Decomposing a strategy handed down from above into your own organization's target states, with an auditor agent.

plugins.name: team-ops
plugins.summary: Team operations on a shared folder as SSoT: knowledge base, backlog and sprints, multi-repo tracking. Needs .claude/team-context.json.

plugins.name: obsidian
plugins.summary: Generic Obsidian helpers (Obsidian Flavored Markdown, Bases, JSON Canvas, CLI). Vault-agnostic - useful in the workhub vault and any other.

plugins.name: persona
plugins.summary: Switchable response personas over a shared token-reduction engine; the app's Persona tab is the only thing that depends on it, and it explains its own absence.

plugins.name: stack-cloudflare
plugins.summary: Cloudflare (Workers, Pages, R2, D1) development helpers.
